newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets rules for finance firms.
newsitem.headline: China sets rules for finance firms.

text.p: The People's Bank of China has issued regulations for financial firms set up by large corporations, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

To set up such financial firms, the corporations must have total assets of at least 1.5 billion yuan, with annual business income in the previous three years of at least five billion yuan and annual profits of at least 200 million yuan, it said.
The minimum assets of the financial firm must be 100 million yuan, it said.
Such firms will mainly offer financial services to their sister firms in credit, settlement, inter-trade borrowing and floating bonds approved by the central bank, it said.
They can offer warranty, credit and consultancy services for their sister companies, it said.
Such firms were banned from trading in stocks, futures or other money-generating products or from buying share rights, equity or corporate bonds that were not issued by their sister firms, it said.
Such firms could only invest in real estate for their own use, it said.
They must obtain the approval of the central bank before trading foreign exchange or securities abroad, it said.
